scoutNotes: The PR claims to fix dailyInterest rounding down to 'round to the nearest cent' by changing Math.floor(x) to Math.round(x*100)/100. That formula actually rounds to the nearest HUNDREDTH of a cent (since balanceCents is already in cents, the extra *100/100 is spurious), so it returns fractional cents like 13.7 instead of the correct nearest-cent value of 14, and the updated tests simply pin the new (wrong) fractional output instead of the value the PR's own stated intent implies. README and docs/security.md ('Amounts are whole cents') are not reconciled with the new fractional-cent behaviour.

confirmed.title: Daily interest scaling bug corrupts balanceCents
confirmed.rootCause: dailyInterest (src/interest.js:13) wraps the result in `Math.round(x * 100) / 100` even though balanceCents/x is already denominated in cents, so it rounds to the nearest 1/100 of a cent rather than the nearest whole cent the docstring, README, and PR title claim — producing fractional balanceCents that violates the integer-cents invariant enforced elsewhere (src/transfers.js:12,43 Number.isInteger checks, src/accounts.js:49 exact-0 close check), drifts further via floating-point error on repeated accrual, and is pinned (not caught) by the updated test at test/interest.test.js:45 whose own expected value (13.7) disproves the 'nearest cent' claim.
confirmed.summary: dailyInterest multiplies an already-cents value by 100 before rounding and divides by 100 after, so it rounds to the nearest 1/100 of a cent (not the nearest cent as the docstring, README and PR title claim), and the fractional-cent result is then added straight onto balanceCents, which every other part of the codebase (src/transfers.js Number.isInteger checks) treats as an integer.
confirmed.failure: dailyInterest(100_000, 500) returns 13.7 (rounded to the nearest 1/100 cent) instead of the nearest-cent value 14; accrueInterest then sets balanceCents to a fractional value (100013.7). Because deposit/transfer enforce Number.isInteger(amountCents) (src/transfers.js:12,43) with no other withdrawal path, a member can reduce the balance only to a non-zero floating remainder (0.6999999999970896 in the simulated case), and closeAccount's exact balanceCents !== 0 check (src/accounts.js:49) then permanently refuses to close that account — the opposite of the PR's stated goal of fixing saver complaints. The updated test/interest.test.js (lines 10 and 27, not line 45 as one of the five sub-citations says) asserts the fractional outputs as expected, so the suite enshrines rather than catches the bug.

sites.title: Daily interest scaling bug corrupts balanceCents
Rounding doesn't match its own "nearest cent" claim
Interest rounds to nearest 1/100 cent, not cent

confirmed.reasoning: Read src/interest.js:11-14 after checkout: dailyInterest computes rawCents = balanceCents*rateBps/10000/365 (already denominated in cents), then does Math.round(rawCents*100)/100 — rounding to the nearest 1/100 of a cent, not the nearest cent the docstring/README/PR title claim. Confirmed with node: raw=13.698630136986301, true nearest-cent (Math.round(raw))=14, but PR formula gives 13.7. Checked src/transfers.js:12 and :43 — both require Number.isInteger(amountCents) for deposit/transfer, and src/accounts.js:49 requires balanceCents !== 0 (exact) to closeAccount, with no other withdrawal path that accepts a fractional/exact-balance amount (confirmed by reading all of accounts.js — closeAccount's only balance check is the strict !==0 guard, and openAccount/setInterestRate have no fractional-amount escape hatch). accrueInterest (src/interest.js:22-36) adds the fractional amount straight onto balanceCents via store.update with no rounding/coercion in store.js (checked src/store.js — update() does a plain merge, no integer enforcement on balanceCents, only transfers.js validates the amountCents argument passed in, not the stored balance). Simulated the real flow: dailyInterest(100_000,500) -> balance becomes 100013.7; withdrawing the max whole-cent amount (100013) leaves remainder 0.6999999999970896 (confirmed via node, matches finder's exact figure), which is neither 0 nor an integer, so closeAccount permanently refuses this account. Ran the actual updated test/interest.test.js with node --test: all 3 tests pass, and the file literally asserts dailyInterest(100_000,500)===13.7 and balanceCents===100_013.7 (lines 10 and 27), i.e. the suite pins the fractional-cent output as 'correct' rather than catching the regression. This is a genuine, diff-introduced defect: the pre-PR code (Math.floor of the already-cents value) was correctly whole-cent; the PR's rewrite is the exact cause. One minor citation note: site (3) names test/interest.test.js:45, but line 45 is the unrelated 'already closed' assertion at file end — the actual pinning assertions are at lines 10 and 27 (as the claim's own 'cited evidence' section correctly says). This is a line-number slip in that one sub-citation, not a flaw in the substance of the claim, which is fully verified.

The scout's four ruled-in angles (correctness, tests-that-dont-test, boundary-contract, data-integrity) only read interest.js/store.js/the tests. The scout's ruled-out 'security' angle explicitly scoped itself to injection/secrets/SSRF/webhooks and never opened docs/security.md, so this explicit, self-declared invariant violation was never checked by any angle.

missed.what: Once an account accrues any fractional-cent interest, it can never be closed again: closeAccount (src/accounts.js:49) requires balanceCents strictly === 0, but transfer and deposit (src/transfers.js:12,43) both require Number.isInteger(amountCents), so no integer withdrawal can ever zero a fractional balance, and no other code path adjusts balance directly. Confirmed by simulation: $1000 at 5% -> balance 100013.7 after one day; withdrawing the max integer 100013 leaves 0.7 cents forever (bal-100000 = 13.69999999999709, never 0). No existing test exercises interest accrual followed by closeAccount.
missed.why: This is a behavioral interaction between interest.js's new output type (float) and an unrelated invariant in accounts.js/transfers.js authored independently of this PR. 'Correctness' examined only dailyInterest's own formula; 'data-integrity' confirmed the store persists the float value correctly (which it does) but didn't follow that value into the account-lifecycle invariant that assumes integers; 'boundary-contract' looked at dailyInterest's own input boundaries (zero/negative), not at a downstream function's equality check; 'tests-that-dont-test' assessed whether the changed assertions test something, not whether an entirely different test file now has an untested interaction. No single angle's framing reaches into accounts.js to find this.
